draft:
**Tidepool Landing Page — Build Plan**

Palette shift for the new brand: deep ocean teal replaces forest green; coral stays (it reads as literal tidepool life). Cream paper background.

1. **Persistent left sidebar — the week rail.** Vertical timeline of Mon–Sun nodes running the full page height, echoing the reference. Nodes fill with coral as the visitor scrolls past sections (Monday = hero, Friday = signup). Clicking a node jumps to that section, framed as "plan the week top to bottom."

2. **Hero.** Headline in the same run-on, breathless voice: *"Bring your whole team together around one living plan for the week that builds itself from everyone's calendar, flags collisions before they happen, and quietly makes the Monday standup optional so nobody ever has to ask what you're working on again."* Screenshot right, ~60/40 split; hand-drawn white arrow curls from headline to a specific UI detail (the conflict-warning badge) with a scribbled annotation: "sees the collision before you do."

3. **How it works — three tides.** Horizontal trio on cream: Sync everyone's calendar → Draft the week together → Adjust live as things shift. Line-art icons in teal; no photography here.

4. **Monospace pull quote.** Full-width teal band. Set in monospace like a terminal/shared-doc line: `"we stopped having planning meetings. the plan is just... there."` — attributed with small circular team avatars, not a corporate headshot.

5. **Proof strip.** Logos of plausible small teams (studios, agencies, open-source projects) rendered as thin teal line-marks, plus one stat in coral: "teams finish planning in 12 minutes."

6. **Closing CTA.** The week rail's Sunday node lands here. "Start your week" button in coral, subcopy: free for teams of five. Footer moon-tide illustration, flat, single-weight teal strokes.

No carousel, no video — the page itself should feel like scrolling through one week.
final:
**Tidepool — Revised Build Plan**

What changed: the week rail stops decorating and starts demonstrating the product; a new "what disappears" section does the persuading; type and color are now specified, not described.

**Design constants.** Cream #FAF6EE base; deep teal #0F4C4C for all text and structure; coral #FF6A5A reserved strictly for interaction and emphasis. Headlines in Fraunces (warm retro-serif), body in Inter, quote in iA Writer Mono.

1. **Week rail — upgraded from tracker to demo.** Mon–Sun nodes down the left edge, each with a tiny mono micro-label ("Mon · plan," "Wed · drift," "Fri · done"), so the sidebar itself previews how a Tidepool week reads. Nodes fill coral on scroll; clicking scrolls you there. On mobile it collapses to a pinned horizontal day strip.

2. **Hero.** Tightened headline, same breathless cadence: *"Bring your whole team around one living plan that assembles itself from everyone's calendars, flags collisions before they land, and quietly makes the Monday standup optional so nobody ever has to ask what you're working on again."* Right side is not a static screenshot — it's a silent looping animation: a task block slides Wednesday→Thursday and a collision badge appears. The hand-drawn arrow points at that badge, annotated: "it saw this before she did."

3. **Three tides.** Sync calendars → draft the week together → adjust live. A thin teal connector line ties each card to the Mon/Wed/Fri rail nodes, so the section literally maps onto the week.

4. **New: What disappears.** Short list, teal text, coral strikethroughs: ~~the Monday standup.~~ ~~the "what are you on?" ping.~~ ~~the Friday recap doc.~~ One line of subcopy: "Tidepool adds nothing to your week. It removes things." Persuasion through subtraction — the strongest fit for the brand voice.

5. **Monospace pull quote.** Styled as a real Tidepool comment artifact: avatar, "edited 9:14 AM," blinking cursor after the last word. *"we stopped having planning meetings. the plan is just... there_"* Full teal band.

6. **Proof strip.** Thin teal line-marks of plausible studios and open-source teams; single coral stat: "average planning session: 12 minutes."

7. **Closing CTA at Sunday.** Inline email input beside a coral "Start your week" button. Subcopy: free up to five people, no card. Footer: flat single-stroke tide illustration.
